messages.author: 1e986504c9c1f16d
messages.subject: sorting with ddply
parts:
Hello,

I'm working with some forest management data and having some
difficulty.

I would like to extract all columns in a dataframe for the eight
largest values of a DBH (diameter at breast height) in each
'site'/'plot'/'time since treatment' combo. I want to compute the mean
height associated with these eight trees with largest diameters. I
have tried using ddply with the helper 'summarise' and sorting the top
eight values of DBH (see code below), but it creates a new dataframe
that does not include the heights associated with these diameters. I
figure using the helper 'subset' would work, but when I use it I get
warnings and a dataframe I'm not looking for. Is there a simple fix to
this, or should I take different approach, perhaps with more steps
involved. Thanks.

m.ht=ddply(trees,.(SITEid,PLOTid,TST),summarise,DBH==sort(DBH,
decreasing=TRUE)[1:8],.progress="text")

m.ht=ddply(trees,.(SITEid,PLOTid,TST),subset,DBH==sort(DBH,
decreasing=TRUE)[1:8],.progress="text")

note: TST is 'time since treatment'

messages.author: 9ff02ee016b8a9e0
messages.subject: Re: sorting with ddply
parts:
I think the problem is you should use '=' instead of '==' in the assignment of the DBH sorted values to the column DBH.

HTH, Scott

Hi Patrick, I think head is the way to go here.

m.ht <- ddply(trees, .(SITEid,PLOTid,TST), function(dtfr)  head(dtfr[order(dtfr$DBH, dec = TRUE), ] , n = 8) ,.progress="text")

HTH
Luciano

treatment', so I can calculate the mean height for those trees.

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: sorting with ddply
parts:
A similar solution is:

ddply(trees, .(SITEid,PLOTid,TST), subset, rank(desc(DBH)) <= 8)

But read the documentation for rank and think carefully about how you
want to deal with ties.

Hadley
